concern.concern: The title, “Conjugating a longitude changes only lower-order Magnus coefficients,” misdescribes the proved statement. With λ=x₁ and u=x₂, conjugation preserves degree one but changes degree two by X₁X₂−X₂X₁. The statement correctly says coefficient changes are integer combinations of lower-order longitude coefficients; the title should express that dependence.

original_concerns.reason: The title asserts which orders change, while the proved statement describes dependence of a degree-m change on lower-degree coefficients. For lambda=x1 and u=x2, multiplying (1+X2)^(-1)(1+X1)(1+X2) through degree two yields degree-two change X1X2-X2X1 and unchanged degree one. This contradicts the title as a description of the result. The existing statement and formal-series proof correctly express dependence on proper contiguous subwords; change the display title only.
